brief.subject: SBA expands SBIC leverage; surety bond rules streamlined
brief.headline: SBA Raises SBIC Leverage Limits and Streamlines Surety Bond Guarantee Rules
brief.dek: Two SBA rules touch small-business financing, the IRS corrects opportunity zone reporting plans, and Florida preparer fraud cases mount.
brief.lede: SBA issued an interim final rule letting SBICs issuing standard debentures access more leverage. That could widen the pool of investment capital for small firms.

sections.heading: SBIC leverage ceiling goes up
bullets: SBA published an interim final rule on SBIC program loan guarantee regulations.
It implements the Investing in All of America Act of 2025, which Congress passed to expand SBIC financing.
SBICs issuing standard debentures can get more leverage, in ratios up to two-to-one.
More fund leverage could mean more capital available to small businesses seeking investment.

sections.heading: Surety bond program gets a cleanup
bullets: SBA finalized changes to its Surety Bond Guarantee program regulations.
Participating surety companies face lighter document submission and retention requirements.
The rule fixes conflicting provisions and updates outdated Preferred Surety admission requirements.
The Quarterly Contract Completion Report is also revised, relevant to contractors relying on SBA-backed bonds.

sections.heading: IRS reporting and hearing updates
bullets: The IRS corrected proposed regulations REG-116506-25 on qualified opportunity zone information reporting.
Those rules would require opportunity funds to file information returns and furnish statements to investors who dispose of interests.
Opportunity zone businesses would furnish statements to the funds holding interests in them.
The December 15, 2026 hearing on the scholarship tax credit proposal is now telephonic-only.

sections.heading: Florida preparers face fraud actions
bullets: Federal authorities have brought a series of enforcement actions against Florida tax preparers.
Preparers are accused of inflating refunds with invented business losses, expenses and deductions.
Clients whose returns carry fabricated deductions can be left exposed to the IRS.

items.title: Rule: Surety Bond Guarantee Program: Streamlining and Modernizing
items.snippet: This final rule makes several changes to the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Surety Bond Guarantee (SBG) program regulations. The rule reduces the burden on participating surety companies for submission and retention of documents. The rule also corrects conflicting provisions, as well as revising the obsolete Preferred Surety admissions requirements and the Quarterly Contract Completion Report.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Information Reporting Regarding Qualified Opportunity Zones and Updated Qualified Opportunity Fund Certification and Decertification Procedures; Correction
items.snippet: This document contains corrections to the proposed regulations (REG-116506-25), published in the Federal Register on September 11, 2026. These proposed regulations would implement new statutory requirements for qualified opportunity funds to file information returns with the IRS and furnish statements to investors who dispose of investments in those entities and for qualified opportunity zone businesses to furnish statements to qualified opportunity funds that hold interests in them.
